original_value: This paper discusses a bi-objective programming of the port-hinterland freight transportation system based on intermodal transportation with the consideration of uncertain transportation demand for green concern. Economic and environmental aspects are integrated in order to obtain green flow distribution solutions for the proposed port-hinterland network. A distributionally robust chance constraint optimization model is then established for the uncertainty of transportation demand, in which the chance constraint is described such that transportation demand is satisfied under the worst-case distribution based on the partial information of the mean and variance. The trade-offs among different objectives and the uncertainty theory applied in the modeling both involve the notion of symmetry. Taking the actual port-hinterland transportation network of the Yangtze River Economic Belt as an example, the results reveal that the railway-road intermodal transport is promoted and the change in total network CO2 emissions is contrary to that in total network costs. Additionally, both network costs and network emissions increase significantly with the growth of the lower bound of probability for chance constraint. The higher the probability level grows, the greater the trade-offs between two objectives are influenced, which indicates that the operation capacity of inland intermodal terminals should be increased to meet the high probability level. These findings can help provide decision supports for the green development strategy of the port-hinterland container transportation network, which meanwhile faces a dynamic planning problem caused by stochastic demands in real life.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines a bi-objective programming approach for a port-hinterland freight transportation system based on intermodal transport, while accounting for uncertain transportation demand in support of green objectives. It integrates economic and environmental considerations to derive green flow distribution solutions for the proposed port-hinterland network. A distributionally robust chance-constrained optimization model is then formulated to address demand uncertainty, with the chance constraint defined so that transportation demand is met under the worst-case distribution using only partial information on the mean and variance. Both the trade-offs among the objectives and the symmetry concept used in the uncertainty modeling involve symmetry. Using the actual port-hinterland transportation network of the Yangtze River Economic Belt as a case study, the results show that railway-road intermodal transport is encouraged and that the change in total network CO2 emissions is opposite to the change in total network costs. In addition, both network costs and emissions rise sharply as the lower bound of the chance-constraint probability increases. As the probability level increases, the trade-off between the two objectives is affected more strongly, indicating that inland intermodal terminal capacity should be expanded to satisfy high probability levels. These findings can provide decision support for the green development strategy of the port-hinterland container transportation network, which in practice also faces a dynamic planning problem caused by stochastic demand.
